finding: A report whose branch_head is a ref name, such as HEAD or story/ST-0350, passes the review check at every later head. check_code_review passes branch_head unchecked to `git merge-base --is-ancestor <branch_head> <branch>`, and git resolves the ref to the current tip, which is always its own ancestor. The review ran this probe in a scratch repository: a report with `branch_head: story/ST-0350` printed PASS code-review. report-format.md requires a full 40-character SHA, so the check accepts a value that the report contract forbids. The behavior looks unintended. The smallest fix is in check_code_review: accept branch_head only when it matches ^[0-9a-f]{40}$, and name the report and the value in the BLOCK line otherwise.
why_this_severity: A report of the story must still exist, so the check still shows that a review ran; only an agent that breaks the report format reaches this path (no to fails_purpose). The ancestor test then says nothing about which commit the review saw, and a later reader cannot tell from the report what was reviewed.
